superior head of lateral pterygoid muscl: Runs from the greater wing of the sphenoid to the articular disc and condyle; steadies the disc as the jaw closes.
superior horn of thyroid cartilage: Upward extension of the thyroid cartilage; joined to the hyoid by the lateral thyrohyoid ligament.
superior mental spine: Upper spine on the inner surface; genioglossus attaches to it.
superior nuchal line: Superior nuchal line; trapezius, SCM and splenius capitis attach to it.
superior oblique muscle: Its tendon passes through the trochlea to attach to the eye; it turns the eye down and out and rotates it inwards. Supplied by the trochlear nerve (IV); when paralysed, double vision appears when going down stairs.
superior pharyngeal constrictor: Constrictor in the wall of the nasopharynx and oropharynx; arises from the pterygomandibular raphe. Pharyngeal plexus (X).
superior pubic ligament: Ligament reinforcing the upper border of the symphysis, extending to the pubic tubercles.
superior pubic ramus: Upper ramus of the pubis; the femoral vessels pass in front of it into the thigh.
superior rectus muscle: Turns the eye up (elevation) and in, and rotates it inwards; supplied by the superior branch of the oculomotor nerve (III).
superior tarsus: Dense connective tissue plate forming the skeleton of the upper eyelid; it contains the meibomian glands.
superior temporal line: Upper line to which the temporal fascia attaches.
superior thyroid notch: V-shaped notch on the upper border of the thyroid cartilage; easily felt in the neck.
superior thyroid tubercle: Prominence at the upper end of the oblique line.
superior transverse scapular ligament: Ligament converting the scapular notch into a foramen; the suprascapular nerve passes beneath it and the suprascapular artery above.
supinator: Muscle wrapping the upper third of the radius; supinates the forearm. The posterior interosseous nerve can be compressed at the arcade of Frohse as it pierces this muscle.
supinator crest: Ridge below the radial notch; supinator arises from it.
supra-acetabular groove: Groove on the upper rim of the acetabulum; the reflected head of rectus femoris attaches to it.
supra-orbital notch: Notch on the upper margin of the orbit; the supraorbital nerve and artery pass through it.
supraglenoid tubercle: Prominence above the glenoid; the long head of biceps arises here.
suprapatellar bursa: Large bursa between the quadriceps tendon and the femur, continuous with the knee joint cavity; it swells in a knee effusion.
supraspinatus muscle: Rotator cuff muscle from the supraspinous fossa to the greater tubercle; initiates the first 15° of abduction. Suprascapular nerve. Its tendon is the one most often torn and impinged.
supraspinous fossa: Fossa above the spine; supraspinatus arises here.
supraspinous ligament: Strong ligament joining the tips of the spinous processes; in the neck it continues as the nuchal ligament.
supreme nuchal line: Highest nuchal line; the galea aponeurotica attaches to it.
surgical neck of humerus: Constriction below the tubercles; it fractures often and the axillary nerve can be injured.
sustentaculum tali: Shelf projecting from the medial surface of the calcaneus; supports the head of the talus, with the FHL tendon passing beneath it.
symphysial surface of pubis: Midline articular surface of the pubis; forms the pubic symphysis with the opposite side.
synovial joints of free lower limb: Synovial joints of free lower limb
synovial joints of free upper limb: Synovial joints of free upper limb
synovial sheaths of digits of hand: Synovial sheaths enclosing the flexor tendons in the fingers; infection (tenosynovitis) requires urgent surgery.
talar sulcus: Groove on the lower surface of the talus; with the calcaneal sulcus it forms the sinus tarsi.
talocalcaneal interosseous ligament: Strong ligament binding the talus and calcaneus within the sinus tarsi; the main stabiliser of the subtalar joint.
talonavicular ligament: Binds the neck of the talus to the upper surface of the navicular.
talus: Tarsal bone transferring weight between leg and foot, with no muscles attached; its trochlea forms the ankle joint. Neck fractures carry a risk of avascular necrosis.
tarsal sinus: Laterally open canal between the talus and calcaneus; contains the interosseous talocalcaneal ligament.
tegmen tympani: Thin bone forming the roof of the middle ear; middle ear infections can spread through it into the skull.
temporal bone: Complex bone housing the middle and inner ear, made up of the petrous, squamous and tympanic parts and the mastoid process; it forms the temporomandibular joint with the mandible.
temporal line: Line on the outer surface of the frontal bone to which the temporal fascia attaches.
temporal surface of frontal bone: Surface forming the front wall of the temporal fossa; temporalis arises here.
temporal surface of greater wing: Surface facing the temporal fossa; temporalis arises here.
temporalis muscle: Fan-shaped muscle from the temporal fossa to the coronoid process; deep temporal nerves (V3). It closes the jaw, and its posterior fibres retract it.
temporoparietalis muscle: Thin, variable muscle of facial expression at the side of the galea.
tendinous arch of levator ani: Thickening of the obturator internus fascia; the line of origin of levator ani.
tendon of extensor digitorum longus: Tendon that splits into four slips on the dorsum of the foot to reach the 2nd–5th toes.
tendon sheath - abd. pollicis longus - e: Sheath around abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis; its narrowing is De Quervain's tenosynovitis (Finkelstein test).
tendon sheath of extensor carpi ulnaris: Tendon sheath of extensor carpi ulnaris
tendon sheath of extensor digiti minimi: Tendon sheath of extensor digiti minimi
tendon sheath of extensor digitorum and: Tendon sheath of extensor digitorum and extensor indicis
